notes.title: 2 Months! + Roadmap 🗺️
notes.content:
It's been two months since release! Wow! Thanks to everyone who's played the game, we're overwhelmed by how many people have been enjoying it. Since release, the dev team's been taking a bit of a break to think about what's next (...when we're not battling the bugs, that is.)

For Mushroom Musume, we have a few new updates planned: a creepy update in October and a lovely update in February. We'll be using these updates to fill out a few stories and collectables we had to cut for time, as well as some improvements we've seen suggested by players! 

Once we've squashed most of the bugs and have those two updates out, we'll begin working on our 'final' update; the main goal of this update will be Steam Workshop integration. We want players to be able to easily mod the game to their mushy heart's content! Mushroom Musume was designed to be pretty easy for people to work with, so it should just take some polish and documentation to open the gates for others to add their own stories or favorite fungal gals.

Other than Mushroom Musume, we're also planning to release a few smaller games over the next year. Our next release on Steam will be a renewed version of our 2022 witchy-feely visual novel [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2937500/Making_Friends/?curator_clanid=45592196]Making Friends [/url](which you can wishlist today!) just in time for Halloween, but we already have ideas a-brewin' for what comes next! So stay tuned~

notes.title: 7/2 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hello! It's been a few days since we've posted an update log for our nightly-ish bug fix builds... here's a list of most of what's been addressed recently!

[list]
[*] We've taken a pass on achievements, some of which were incorrectly triggering (or not triggering) previously. We also got approval from Steam for more achievements, so in the coming weeks we'll be filling in some we had to cut before launch!
[*] Remaining bugs affecting the garden and garden items have been dealt with. If you had issues with your garden refusing to grow or difficulties with item quantities or spores from Gnome Depot, then give it another try.
[*] Various crashes from around the game have been fixed.
[*] An ending wasn't being triggered correctly previously, and should now be gettable.
[*] Clicking whilst lines with a 'typewriter effect' would previously cause the line to be skipped, now it should correctly complete the animation on the text instead.
[*] Controller support has been improved for combat events
[*] The code managing first-person dungeon navigation has been refactored, hopefully resulting in a more stable experience. (This is an ongoing effort, with more improvements coming in the future as well!)
[*] ...and a couple of other little things we're forgetting about, I'm sure~
[/list]

Thanks, as always, for playing! If you run into anything unexpected, feel free to let us know through our [url=https://forms.gle/sVqb8fB568JGVWzRA]bug submission forum[/url] (or the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2484580/discussions/0/603033962491702883/]pinned topic[/url] in the Steam discussion forum).

notes.title: Check Out Mushroom Musume at Next Fest!
notes.content:
[h1]Hot Off the Presses![/h1]

While the team is hard at work finishing up some expanded content for the full release, we've also taken the time to whip up a new build that everyone can enjoy just in time for Next Fest (live now~)

This new build features a variety of small bug fixes, as well as an updated Settings menu (with new display options) to allow for maximum comfort while rearing mushroom children.

Stay tuned for news about the full release... We've been holding off on officially announcing the release date until things are mostly ready, but I think we're on track for our internal goal at least!

notes.title: This weekend I grew a fungus daughter in eerie narrative RPG Mushroom Musume, which has a demo
notes.content:
I don't plan on having kids, but in the event that I change my mind, commissioning a forest Witch to grow one from a mushroom seems a lot easier than the usual human procreative process, though possibly just as abundant in screaming. I've been playing the demo for "cute-creepy" RPG and life sim Mushroom Musume, in which you - an unnamed "Recluse" - cultivate and play as a series of mushroom daughters. My current mushroom daughter is called Alia. She's a Common Turquoise Truffle. She's got a small pig acquaintance, who so far hasn't tried to devour her, and a cute fuzzy hat, which she stole from outside a church - precise impact on character development still TBC.
